pattern: Ranked-order throwing/scoring reconstruction from partial throw results
context_passage:
10 players (P1 best going in) compete in javelin over 6 rounds in two phases (1-3, then 4-6). A player's score is his best valid throw so far. Phase-1 rounds throw in increasing rank order; top 6 qualify for Phase 2, throwing in decreasing rank order. Ranks 1,2,3 at Round 6 win gold, silver, bronze.

Round 1 valid throws: P1=82.9, P3=81.5, P5=86.4, P6=82.5, P7=87.2, P9=84.1.
Round 3 valid throws: P1=88.6, P3=79.0, P9=81.4.

i. In Round 2, only the last two throws were valid; both qualified, one with the least score. Neither medalled.
ii. A 'double' = throwing first in a round having thrown last the previous round. Two players got a double.
iii. In each Phase-2 round, exactly one player improved, each improvement equal.
iv. Gold, bronze improved in Rounds 5, 6; one medalist improved in Round 4.
v. Gold-Silver gap = Silver-Bronze gap = 1.0 m.
question_text: Which two players got the double?
explanation:
Round-1 ranks give the Round-2 throwing order P7,P5,P9,P1,P6,P3,P2,P4,P8,P10. Only P8's (9th) and P10's (last) throws were valid.

P10 must overtake P7 to become rank-1 (throwing first in Round 3) — since he was also last in Round 2, this gives him a double. P8 ends as the lowest qualifier and, by the Round 3→4 phase transition, is also the last qualifier to throw in Round 3 and first in Round 4 — a double too.

pattern: Threshold-based mixture testing — bounding impurity from a detection threshold
context_passage: Each bottle holds 50 ml of liquid, either 100% pure (P) or with some impurity (I), visually indistinguishable. A testing device detects impurity only if it makes up 10% or more of the tested content. For example, mixing 10 ml of pure liquid with 20 ml of 80%-P/20%-I liquid gives a detectable mixture, but mixing 10 ml of pure liquid with 5 ml of the same impure liquid does not.
question_text: 5 ml of content from bottle A is mixed with 5 ml of content from bottle B. The resultant mixture, when tested, detects the presence of I. If it is known that bottle A contains only P, what BEST can be concluded about the volume of I in bottle B?
explanation:
Let x be the impurity fraction in bottle B. A 5 ml sample from B carries 5x ml of I; mixed with 5 ml pure A, the mixture's impurity fraction is x/2.

Detection requires x/2 ≥ 10%, so x ≥ 20%. Bottle B holds 50 ml total, so its actual I volume is at least 10 ml.
